papers.title: Concurrent Learning of Policy and Unknown Safety Constraints in Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has revolutionized decision-making across a wide range of domains over the past few decades. Yet, deploying RL policies in real-world scenarios presents the crucial challenge of ensuring safety. Traditional safe RL approaches have predominantly focused on incorporating predefined safety constraints into the policy learning process. However, this reliance on predefined safety constraints poses limitations in dynamic and unpredictable real-world settings where such constraints may not be available or sufficiently adaptable. Bridging this gap, we propose a novel approach that concurrently learns a safe RL control policy and identifies the unknown safety constraint parameters of a given environment. Initializing with a parametric signal temporal logic (pSTL) safety specification and a small initial labeled dataset, we frame the problem as a bilevel optimization task, intricately integrating constrained policy optimization, using a Lagrangian-variant of the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm, with Bayesian optimization for optimizing parameters for the given pSTL safety specification. Through experimentation in comprehensive case studies, we validate the efficacy of this approach across varying forms of environmental constraints, consistently yielding safe RL policies with high returns. Furthermore, our findings indicate successful learning of STL safety constraint parameters, exhibiting a high degree of conformity with true environmental safety constraints. The performance of our model closely mirrors that of an ideal scenario that possesses complete prior knowledge of safety constraints, demonstrating its proficiency in accurately identifying environmental safety constraints and learning safe policies that adhere to those constraints.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注强化学习中的安全约束学习，与FEA代理模型或植入物设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, or biomechanics design; it focuses on safe RL with unknown constraints.

summary_zh.motivation: 在动态环境中，预定义安全约束不足，需要同时学习策略和未知约束。
summary_zh.method: 将约束策略优化与贝叶斯优化结合，学习pSTL安全规范参数。
summary_zh.result: 方法能有效学习安全约束并生成高回报的安全策略。
summary_zh.validation: 通过多种环境约束的案例研究验证有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To address the limitation of predefined safety constraints in dynamic environments by concurrently learning a safe RL policy and unknown safety constraint parameters.
summary_en.method: A bilevel optimization framework integrating constrained policy optimization (Lagrangian-variant TD3) with Bayesian optimization to learn parametric STL safety specifications.
summary_en.result: The approach consistently yields safe RL policies with high returns and accurately identifies environmental safety constraints.
summary_en.validation: Validated through comprehensive case studies with varying environmental constraints.

papers.title: A novel data generation scheme for surrogate modelling with deep operator networks
papers.abstract: Operator-based neural network architectures such as DeepONets have emerged as a promising tool for the surrogate modeling of physical systems. In general, towards operator surrogate modeling, the training data is generated by solving the PDEs using techniques such as Finite Element Method (FEM). The computationally intensive nature of data generation is one of the biggest bottleneck in deploying these surrogate models for practical applications. In this study, we propose a novel methodology to alleviate the computational burden associated with training data generation for DeepONets. Unlike existing literature, the proposed framework for data generation does not use any partial differential equation integration strategy, thereby significantly reducing the computational cost associated with generating training dataset for DeepONet. In the proposed strategy, first, the output field is generated randomly, satisfying the boundary conditions using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). From the output field, the input source field can be calculated easily using finite difference techniques. The proposed methodology can be extended to other operator learning methods, making the approach widely applicable. To validate the proposed approach, we employ the heat equations as the model problem and develop the surrogate model for numerous boundary value problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种无需求解PDE即可生成DeepONet训练数据的方法，可显著降低代理模型的计算成本，对生物力学植入物设计中的高效采样具有潜在迁移价值。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not address constraints, uncertainty quantification, or implant/biomechanics design; it only demonstrates on heat equations without biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低DeepONet训练数据生成的计算成本
summary_zh.method: 用高斯过程回归随机生成满足边界条件的输出场，再通过有限差分反算输入场
summary_zh.result: 无需求解PDE即可生成训练数据，显著降低计算开销
summary_zh.validation: 以热方程为例验证代理模型精度

summary_en.motivation: To alleviate the computational burden of generating training data for DeepONet surrogate models by avoiding PDE integration.
summary_en.method: Randomly generate output fields satisfying boundary conditions via Gaussian Process Regression, then compute input source fields using finite differences.
summary_en.result: The proposed data generation scheme eliminates the need for PDE solvers, drastically reducing computational cost while maintaining surrogate accuracy.
summary_en.validation: Validated on heat equation boundary value problems, demonstrating comparable performance to traditional data generation.

papers.title: PhyPlan: Compositional and Adaptive Physical Task Reasoning with Physics-Informed Skill Networks for Robot Manipulators
papers.abstract: Given the task of positioning a ball-like object to a goal region beyond direct reach, humans can often throw, slide, or rebound objects against the wall to attain the goal. However, enabling robots to reason similarly is non-trivial. Existing methods for physical reasoning are data-hungry and struggle with complexity and uncertainty inherent in the real world. This paper presents PhyPlan, a novel physics-informed planning framework that combines physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with modified Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to enable embodied agents to perform dynamic physical tasks. PhyPlan leverages PINNs to simulate and predict outcomes of actions in a fast and accurate manner and uses MCTS for planning. It dynamically determines whether to consult a PINN-based simulator (coarse but fast) or engage directly with the actual environment (fine but slow) to determine optimal policy. Evaluation with robots in simulated 3D environments demonstrates the ability of our approach to solve 3D-physical reasoning tasks involving the composition of dynamic skills. Quantitatively, PhyPlan excels in several aspects: (i) it achieves lower regret when learning novel tasks compared to state-of-the-art, (ii) it expedites skill learning and enhances the speed of physical reasoning, (iii) it demonstrates higher data efficiency compared to a physics un-informed approach.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文将PINN用于机器人物理推理，而非生物力学或植入物设计中的有限元代理建模。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA surrogate modeling for biomedical implants, no constraint handling, no uncertainty quantification, and no biomechanics context.

summary_zh.motivation: 机器人物理推理任务复杂且数据需求高，现有方法难以处理现实世界的不确定性。
summary_zh.method: 结合PINN与蒙特卡洛树搜索，动态选择PINN模拟或真实环境交互以规划最优策略。
summary_zh.result: 在3D物理推理任务中，该方法降低了学习新任务的遗憾，提高了数据效率和推理速度。
summary_zh.validation: 在模拟3D环境中进行机器人任务评估，与基线方法对比。

summary_en.motivation: Robots struggle with complex physical reasoning tasks due to data hunger and real-world uncertainty, requiring efficient and adaptive planning.
summary_en.method: PhyPlan integrates physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with modified Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to dynamically decide between coarse PINN simulation and fine real-world interaction for optimal policy.
summary_en.result: The framework achieves lower regret, faster skill learning, and higher data efficiency than state-of-the-art methods in simulated 3D physical reasoning tasks.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated in simulated 3D environments with robot manipulation tasks, comparing regret and learning speed against baselines.

papers.title: Batch Active Learning of Reward Functions from Human Preferences
papers.abstract: Data generation and labeling are often expensive in robot learning. Preference-based learning is a concept that enables reliable labeling by querying users with preference questions. Active querying methods are commonly employed in preference-based learning to generate more informative data at the expense of parallelization and computation time. In this paper, we develop a set of novel algorithms, batch active preference-based learning methods, that enable efficient learning of reward functions using as few data samples as possible while still having short query generation times and also retaining parallelizability. We introduce a method based on determinantal point processes (DPP) for active batch generation and several heuristic-based alternatives. Finally, we present our experimental results for a variety of robotics tasks in simulation. Our results suggest that our batch active learning algorithm requires only a few queries that are computed in a short amount of time. We showcase one of our algorithms in a study to learn human users' preferences.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究机器人学习中基于人类偏好的奖励函数批量主动学习，与FEA代理建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on preference-based reward learning for robotics, with no connection to finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少机器人学习中偏好标注的数据需求
summary_zh.method: 提出基于行列式点过程的批量主动查询方法
summary_zh.result: 少量查询即可高效学习奖励函数
summary_zh.validation: 在多种仿真机器人任务中验证

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the number of human preference queries needed for learning reward functions in robotics.
summary_en.method: Proposes batch active learning algorithms using determinantal point processes and heuristics to select informative queries.
summary_en.result: The batch active methods achieve efficient reward learning with few queries and short computation times.
summary_en.validation: Validated on simulated robotics tasks and a human user study.
